title: Number Bases: Binary and Other Bases
seo_title: Number Bases – JSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Convert numbers from base ten to other bases and from other bases to base ten; add, subtract and multiply binary numbers. (summary of the NERDC JSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 1 maths worksheets on number bases: converting between base ten and bases two to eight, and adding, subtracting and multiplying binary numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Place values in base b: 1, b, b², b³
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In base two the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, … In base five they are 1, 5, 25, 125, …
  • To change to base ten, multiply each digit by its place value and add.
  • To change from base ten, divide by the base repeatedly and read the remainders upwards. In binary, 1 + 1 = 10₂ and 1 + 1 + 1 = 11₂.

Examples

Example

1011₂ + 111₂

11 + 7 = 18

Answer: 10010₂

Example

101₂ × 11₂

5 × 3 = 15

Answer: 1111₂

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Carrying 10 in binaryCarry when you reach 2.
Reading remainders downwardsRead from the bottom up.
Using digits as big as the baseBase five has no digit 5.

items.e: Multiply each digit by its place value (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32): 1 × 16 + 1 × 8 + 1 × 4 + 1 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 31.

items.q: Change 38 to a binary number (base two).
items.e: Divide by 2 again and again: 38 ÷ 2 = 19 remainder 0; 19 ÷ 2 = 9 remainder 1; 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1; 4 ÷ 2 = 2 remainder 0; 2 ÷ 2 = 1 remainder 0; 1 ÷ 2 = 0 remainder 1. Read the remainders from the bottom up: 100110₂.
